claim: viva-genicam implements GVCP ACTION_CMD (opcode 0x0100) including scheduled action commands (64-bit action time, flag bit 7) and exposes it in Python as viva_genicam.send_action(device_key, group_key, group_mask, scheduled_time=None, destination='255.255.255.255', timeout_ms=200); a fake camera acked only when keys matched.

how_verified: read-code + ran-test (Frame attributes ts_dev/ts_host printed in Docker test)

claim: Aravis (LGPL-2.1+, last tag 0.9.2 on 2026-04-23, HEAD 2026-10-22) does not implement the GVCP ACTION_CMD; its GVCP command enum covers only discovery, bye, packet resend, read/write register/memory and pending ack. Consequently aravis-rs and aravissrc cannot send action commands.

The GStreamer aravissrc element works against a GigE Vision device (tested 0.8.30 from Ubuntu 24.04, which ships libgstaravis.0.8.so in libaravis-0.8-0); Aravis main (unreleased, commit ee31d82f1 on 2026-10-03) adds add-reference-timestamp-meta that attaches the absolute device timestamp as timestamp/x-ptp reference meta.
how_verified: ran-test: gst-launch-1.0 aravissrc camera-name=127.0.0.1 num-buffers=5 ! fakesink -> caps video/x-bayer bggr 512x512, EOS; read-code + git log -S

claim: rc_genicam_api (BSD-3 Roboception code + EMVA GenICam reference implementation + bundled closed-source Baumer GigE/USB GenTL producer v2.9.2 under a Baumer EULA) targets Linux and Windows only (no macOS), describes itself as for GigE Vision 2.0 compatible cameras, and its gc_config tool toggles PtpEnable and reads PtpStatus/PtpOffsetFromMaster after PtpDataSetLatch.

Basler's pylon EULA (Version 137, 2026-10-19) restricts use to operating Basler camera products (§4) and limits redistribution; pypylon (BSD-3 wrapper, 26.9 on 2026-10-23) has wheels for Windows, macOS (arm64/x86_64, macOS 14+) and Linux x86_64/aarch64.

claim: Basler PTP is IEEE 1588-2008 configured via GevIEEE1588/GevIEEE1588DataSetLatch/GevIEEE1588Status/GevIEEE1588OffsetFromMaster (or PtpEnable/PtpDataSetLatch/PtpServoStatus on ace 2 and dart M); action commands use ActionDeviceKey/ActionGroupKey/ActionGroupMask with TriggerSource=Action1 and are sent with IGigETransportLayer::IssueActionCommand.

Teledyne FLIR Spinnaker states support for FLIR and Dalsa cameras (no third-party statement), runs on Windows 11, Ubuntu 20.04-24.04, macOS and Linux ARM64, and downloads require login; Blackfly S PTP is enabled via TransportLayerControl/GigEVision/GevIEEE1588 and GevIEEE1588Mode, with ptp4l recommended as host master.

Allied Vision Vimba X (2026-3) explicitly supports GenICam-compliant cameras and transport layers from all manufacturers free of charge; VmbPy is BSD-2, PyPI vmbpy 1.2.3 (2026-10-06) has wheels only for Linux x86_64/aarch64 and win_amd64, does not include transport layers, and sends action commands via the Interface's ActionDeviceKey/GroupKey/GroupMask + ActionCommand.run().
how_verified: read-spec/doc + read-code (cloned VmbPy) + PyPI JSON API

claim: LUCID Arena SDK is documented as supporting LUCID GigE Vision cameras on Windows, Linux and ARM (no macOS); LUCID's PTP sync recipe uses device-nodemap features PtpEnable, PtpSlaveOnly, PtpStatus, PtpDataSetLatch/PtpDataSetLatchValue, TransferControlMode=UserControlled, TriggerSource=Action0, ActionUnconditionalMode, and ActionCommandFireCommand for scheduled action commands.

Pleora eBUS SDK 7.0 works with any GigE Vision device but requires a Developer Seat license and a GEV-Rx receiver runtime license for non-Pleora devices, otherwise an embossed watermark is applied; no macOS support is listed.
Ubuntu 24.04 packages arv-fake-gv-camera-0.8 in 'aravis-tools' (not 'aravis-tools-cli'); the Aravis fake camera exposes no GevIEEE1588/PtpEnable nodes, so it cannot be used to test PTP configuration.
how_verified: ran-test: dpkg -L aravis-tools; arv-tool-0.8 -a 127.0.0.1 control GevIEEE1588 PtpEnable -> "Feature not found"
